solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support fool, one with attitude

parts.note: an ass is a fool
I is the Roman numeral for one
a stance is an attitude or position taken

explanation.surface: Someone backs an idiot who has a bit of an attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is help or backing, a synonym of support as a noun.

clue.text: Performer in part is tame

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: An actor whose role is a docile one.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist can be any performer or entertainer, as in a variety artist.

clue.text: Plant a kiss after short look suggesting happiness

indicators.note: after says the kiss comes behind the shortened look
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a smile is a look that suggests happiness
X is the symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: Someone plants a kiss after a brief cheerful glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims SMILE to SMIL; 'Plant' reads as a verb but is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Smilax is a genus of climbing plants, including sarsaparilla.

clue.text: Vehicles that might upset tar-smeller so?

indicators.note: might upset suggests the letters could be tipped over into another order

explanation.surface: Road-building machines could be unsettling to someone who sniffs tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might upset' rearranges the letters of TAR-SMELLER and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamrollers are heavy road vehicles used for flattening surfaces.

clue.text: Some land? A group of sailors will get the women coming out

indicators.note: coming out says the women's letter leaves the word

parts.note: a crew is a group of sailors
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A ship's company finds the women leaving when they reach land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' takes W from CREW to leave CRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a measure of land, so it is a certain amount of land.

clue.text: Say, I will get put in order in an establishment like Oxford University!

definitions.text: in an establishment like Oxford University!

indicators.note: will get means the ordering word receives the other letters inside it

parts.note: to collate is to put in order
EG, for example, is signalled by 'say'

explanation.surface: A student says he will be sorted out once he is at an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example'; 'will get' is the container signal, the ordering verb receiving the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Collegiate describes life within a university made up of colleges, as Oxford is.

clue.text: Discharge sets the enemy into retreat

indicators.note: sending a word into retreat makes it go backwards, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: time is proverbially 'the enemy', as in the phrase 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: Something discharged forces the foe to pull back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into retreat' turns TIME round to give the answer; 'the enemy' is the proverbial label for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or send out, a synonym of discharge as a verb.

clue.text: Big circle established by fellow, including Queen and dictator

indicators.note: including means the first piece takes the others inside it

parts.note: a man is a fellow
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: A great ring set up by a man with a monarch and a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A meridian is a great circle of the earth passing through both poles.

clue.text: Conjecture with nothing right is accepted by you

indicators.note: accepted by means the earlier pieces are taken inside the later one

parts.note: thee is an old form of you
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Guessing with no correct answer is something you put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form a theory, a synonym of conjecture as a verb.

clue.text: Paper in circulation that won't get read!

definitions.text: Paper in circulation that won't get read!

parts.words: Paper in circulation that won't get read!
parts.note: sounds like a newspaper on general sale, but it is paper on a roll that goes round and round, used in the bathroom and never read

explanation.definitionFit: This household paper is wound in a roll and used in the lavatory, never read like a newspaper.

clue.text: Language used by writers elsewhere

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tongue employed by authors in other places.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Get clean room organised for business group

indicators.note: organised says the letters are arranged in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A firm's instruction to have the office tidied up.
explanation.definitionFit: A conglomerate is a corporation made of many diverse businesses.

clue.text: Obsequious host, society male to the fore

parts.note: a host is a great multitude, especially an army

explanation.surface: A fawning party host, a gentleman of society out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the fore' puts S and M before ARMY; 'host' means a multitude, not someone throwing a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes an oily, ingratiating manner, much the same as obsequious.

clue.text: Viewer is more apt to speak out when he churns over inside

indicators.note: inside says the turned word sits within the other piece

parts.words: is more apt to speak out
parts.note: someone more apt to speak out is bolder

indicators.note: churning a word over turns it upside down in a down sense, so here it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An onlooker becomes more outspoken when his stomach churns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churns over' sounds like a stomach turning but signals the reversal of 'he', and 'inside' sets the turned pronoun within the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: A beholder is one who looks at or sees something, as in 'the eye of the beholder'.

clue.text: Actress to rage when upset about dress

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the other piece
when upset says the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: garb is dress or clothing

explanation.surface: A film star flies into a tantrum over a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' turns TO RAGE into GRETAO, and 'about' puts it round GARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film actress of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Possibly drop in bags as requirement if you're flying

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Maybe you deposit luggage before taking a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges all the letters of DROP IN BAGS AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Airline passengers must show this card at the gate to get on the aircraft.

clue.text: Detective finds last of clues — the woman's hair

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the following word

parts.note: her is the possessive for the woman
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: An investigator finds the final clue: a strand of her hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes is the fictional detective created by Arthur Conan Doyle.

clue.text: Old boy with old language carrying old ecclesiastical offering

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: carrying means the language holds the extra letter inside it

parts.note: Latin is an old language

explanation.surface: A former pupil with a classical tongue bears an antique church gift.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblation is a thing presented to God, an offering in church worship.

clue.text: Qualification obtained by learner, one in residence

indicators.note: in says the learner and the one go within the residence

parts.note: a habitation is a place of residence
L is the abbreviation for learner, from L-plates
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A certificate gained by a student living in college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained by' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Habilitation is a postdoctoral academic qualification in many European countries, so it is a kind of qualification.

clue.text: It sounds like you need a sleep? Stop

indicators.note: it sounds like says the answer is said the same way as the next words

parts.note: a sleep is a rest

explanation.surface: A tired person is told to stop for a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you need' is a link; 'a rest' said aloud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest is to halt or check, a synonym of stop.

clue.text: More successful person taking risks for financial gain?

definitions.meaning: comparative of good, meaning doing well than another

definitions.text: person taking risks for financial gain?
definitions.meaning: a gambler, one who places wagers

explanation.definitionFit: Better is the comparative of good, and also a noun for someone who bets money.

clue.text: A rare dog going wild — a problem for a driver

indicators.note: going wild says the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncommon hound running loose causes trouble on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is uncontrolled anger shown by motorists, a known hazard of driving.

clue.text: Beloved to pass away clutching part of body

indicators.note: clutching means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: to die is to pass away
the ear is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A loved one dying while grasping some part of their anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearie is an affectionate form of address meaning darling or loved one.

clue.text: Former Wimbledon champion in a women's magazine

parts.note: She was a British women's magazine

explanation.surface: A one-time tennis champion appears in a magazine for women.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE was a British monthly women's magazine; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe won the men's singles at Wimbledon in 1975.

clue.text: Stewed dish in book, not starter

indicators.note: not starter says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a folio is a large book

explanation.surface: A recipe for a casserole found in a cookbook, but no first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starter' drops F from FOLIO; the surface suggests a menu without an appetiser.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a spicy Spanish or Portuguese stew of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Publicist here admits flop

indicators.note: admits means the first piece lets the second in

parts.note: to be present is to be here
to sag is to droop or flop

explanation.surface: A PR person here owns up to a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' is the container signal; 'flop' looks like a noun for a failure but is the verb meaning droop.
explanation.definitionFit: A press agent is employed to get publicity for a client, a publicist by another name.

clue.text: Relations known primarily for creating a little difficulty?

parts.note: kin are one's relations

indicators.note: primarily means taking just the leading letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Family members famed chiefly for stirring up minor trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A kink is a small snag or flaw in a plan, a minor difficulty to iron out.

clue.text: Bird that could be in competition with Winnie?

definitions.text: Bird that could be in competition with Winnie?

parts.words: Bird that could be in competition with Winnie?
parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh loves honey, so a bird that feeds on honey would be his rival for it

explanation.definitionFit: This Australasian songbird feeds on nectar, and its name reflects that sweet diet like Pooh's.
